transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-07 14:30 UTC | Duration: 47 mins
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Anita Gomez (Redwood SE), David Ortega (CISO, Vanguard), Priya Nair (Head of Infra), Liam Brooks (Security Ops), Maya Patel (Cloud Architect)

--- Auto-summary (brief) ---
Sofia: quick overview, then deep dive on incident response and BCDR. Customer wanted RTO/RPO numbers and proof points for failover.

00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick off. I'm Sofia with Redwood, Marcus and Anita from our security/infra team. David, Priya, you good to go?
00:08 David: Yeah thanks, thanks. We're mainly focused today on incident response and bcd r, plus SLA. we have some constraints around data residency and on-prem options so want to make sure the playbooks line up.
00:18 Marcus: Great. Outline - SOC 2 / ISO posture, audit logs, encryption/KMS, then incident response + BCDR specifics: RTO/RPO, sla targets, escalation.
00:30 Priya: Quick ask — we run on multi-region GCP and have a DR window centered on weekend maintenance. Need to know if Redwood's Dedicated can meet our RTO of 15 minutes for critical inference endpoints.
00:45 Marcus: Ok quick qualifier — are critical endpoints running on Redwood Dedicated or Private?
00:50 Maya: We're evaluating both Dedicated and Private VPC. For now pilot on Dedicated reserved GPUs then potentially private.
01:00 Anita: For Dedicated we offer reserved pools with predictable throughput; our documented RTO for a single-region failure with cross-region failover is 10-30 minutes depending on model size and KV-cache warm-up. For smaller seq lengths and pre-warmed KV cache it's typically under 15.
01:20 Liam: When you say KV cache, do you mean the key value cache warm-up? we've seen a lot of variation there.
01:25 Marcus: Yep, kv cache yes — there's some transcription in our docs as KV cache. The warm-up is the main factor. If you use prefix caching and keep a hot replica in the DR region the effective RTO drops significantly.
01:40 David: What's your RPO? we need to confirm no loss of context for sessions in flight.
01:46 Anita: RPO for in-flight tokens depends — for real-time inference we recommend stateless requests or client-side checkpointing. For session-based flows we have options: replicate KV snapshots every 30s-5m. Typical RPO we can commit to is 1 minute for enterprise Dedicated with cross-region replication enabled, but that requires network egress and storage replication and has cost implications.
02:10 Priya: Ok that's helpful. Can you show where that lives in the SLA doc?
02:15 Sofia: We'll send the SLA matrix after the call — it has tiers. Our standard hosted SLA is 99.9% with best-effort failover. Dedicated enterprise SLA can be 99.95% with agreed runbooks and a DR test schedule.
02:33 David: Penalties or crediting? how are outages handled?
02:36 Marcus: The contract contains service credits tied to monthly uptime percentage. For 99.95 vs 99.9 difference we have sliding credit scale; we'll attach the full table.
02:49 Maya: For security we need details on escalation: who gets paged, SLA for response, and on-call rotation details.
02:55 Anita: Our incident response has 3 tiers — detection & triage, remediation, and post-mortem. Notification to customer is immediate upon detection of a Sev-1 affecting customer, we provide an initial incident post within 15 minutes and an update cadence every 30 minutes until mitigation. On-call roster is available in the contract appendix.
03:15 Liam: Are these runbooks public or redacted? we'd like to see the playbook for network partition and for compromised keys.
03:22 Marcus: We can share redacted runbook versions — full internal playbooks contain vendor and internal tooling references. Redacted versions include escalation paths, SLAs, and contact points.
03:33 David: About compromised keys — what is your KMS model? do you provide HSM-backed keys or do we bring our own?
03:38 Anita: Both. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS; enterprise Dedicated/Private can integrate with customer-managed KMS via KMIP or cloud KMS (GCP KMS, AWS KMS). For highest assurance we support HSM-backed keys through partner integrations.
03:54 Priya: And audit logs — how long do you retain logs and can we ship to our SIEM?
04:00 Marcus: Audit logs are retained by default 90 days in the control plane; we support configurable retention up to 7 years for enterprise packages. Logs can be streamed to your SIEM via syslog or secure S3 export with encryption in transit. We also provide immutable event records for compliance.
04:20 Maya: Are logs redacted for PII?
04:23 Anita: We redact PII in control plane logs; request/response payloads are not stored unless you opt into session logging for debugging. For enterprise we can do tokenization or redaction pipelines before export.
04:36 David: On SSO/RBAC — we need SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO, and fine-grained RBAC so operators can't access data plane.
04:44 Marcus: We support SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning for user sync. RBAC supports role-bound policies and can be scoped to projects or model routes; admin vs operator separation is standard. For private deployments you can enforce network-level restrictions so data plane is only accessible within your VPC.
05:01 Liam: Great. A couple of specifics — in a Sev-1 data-plane incident, who is escalation owner? how do we escalate to exec level?
05:09 Anita: Triage owner is the SE on-call; if not resolved in 30 minutes it escalates to the infra lead and then to a dedicated incident commander; exec-level engagement is triggered if impact extends beyond 2 hours or if data exfiltration is suspected. We will share the contact matrix.
05:26 David: Can we get a named exec contact for SLA breach?
05:29 Sofia: Yes we can list named execs in ELA/contract with corresponding escalation SLAs.
05:35 Priya: Testing — we want to run a DR test that simulates region outage for a subset of endpoints. What's your approach and expected customer impact?
05:44 Marcus: We propose a scheduled DR window, Redwood to create a shadow failover with traffic cutover for non-prod first. For Dedicated we can run warm failover where a secondary pool is pre-warmed. Expected impact: short 30-90s ramp as DNS and LB changes propagate if not using sticky session proxying; if using pre-warmed replica impacts are near-zero for stateless calls. We'll coordinate maintenance windows.
06:12 Maya: DNS TTL and client retry logic will matter.
06:14 Anita: Correct. We'll provide recommended client-side retry/backoff patterns.
06:18 David: About encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between customer components and Redwood data plane?
06:22 Marcus: mTLS is supported for Private deployments. For Dedicated we provide TLS mutual auth options and client certs for higher assurance.
06:31 Liam: Key rotation — how is that handled?
06:33 Anita: Keys can be rotated by schedule via KMS and we support seamless rotation for model encryption keys; for long-running sessions we recommend short-lived session keys or a rekey handshake to avoid interruption. We'll send our key rotation policy.
06:50 Priya: A question on data residency — we need EU-only processing for certain customers. Is that available?
06:55 Sofia: Yes, we have region pinning and can guarantee EU-only processing on Dedicated/Private deployments. Hosted API for sensitive data can also be routed to EU-only regions with contractual data residency clauses.
07:10 David: Following up on incident postmortems — do you share RCA with timelines and mitigations?
07:15 Marcus: Yes, postmortems include timeline, root cause analysis, customer impact, and corrective action plan. For high-severity incidents we commit to a 10-business-day initial RCA and follow-up.
07:27 Maya: Can we require a tabletop/test within the first 90 days of onboarding?
07:30 Sofia: Absolutely, we typically recommend a tabletop within 30-60 days and a full DR run by 90 days. We'll include that in the onboarding plan.
07:40 David: One more: SLA credits — how do customers claim them?
07:43 Marcus: Customers file a claim via support portal with evidence; credits are applied to next billing cycle. We can also automate detection and flagging for some classes of incidents.
07:54 Liam: Any residual question about compliance frameworks — do you have an SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate?
08:00 Sofia: Yes we have both SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. We'll share redacted copies and mapping to control requirements.
08:08 Priya: Perfect.

-- Mid-call clarifications / small talk (~08:15 to 12:00) --
08:15 David: How often do you run internal DR drills?
08:20 Anita: Quarterly tabletop and at least one live failover drill annually for infra teams.
08:28 Maya: Any public status history?
08:30 Marcus: We have status.redwood.ai for incident history and public postmortems for major incidents; private customers also get a secure feed and historical uptime reports.

12:15 David: Let's talk about legal / evidence for audits — can we get exportable logs and encryption proofs?
12:22 Anita: Yes, we support time-stamped audit exports with signatures, and we can provide key custody attestations for KMS. Also support for HSM attestation if needed.
12:35 Priya: For the DR testing, we'll need a test plan and breaker checklist.
12:39 Marcus: We'll author a test plan template and include a breaker checklist and rollback options.

25:00 Sofia: Quick recap before we close — action items: send SOC2 & ISO artifacts, SLA matrix, incident runbook redacted, propose DR test dates.
25:10 David: Sounds good. Also please include the escalation contact list and an example postmortem.
25:18 Sofia: We'll include. Any final Qs?
25:22 Liam: One more — for data plane compromise scenario, what is the communication cadence to customers?
25:26 Anita: Immediate notification, initial summary within 15 minutes, hourly updates until containment, full RCA within 10 business days, and mitigations.
25:40 David: Thanks. We'll review artifacts and propose dates for the tabletop.
25:47 Sofia: Great — we'll follow up with an email and attach docs. Thanks all.

--- End meeting ---

Notes: transcript contains some imperfect ASR words (KV cache spelled as 'kv cache') and occasional speaker label shifts. References to product names: Dedicated, Private, Redwood. Shared artifacts: link placeholders - /redwood/security/soc2.pdf, /redwood/sla/matrix.xlsx, /redwood/runbooks/redacted-incident-runbook.pdf
